evidence: ai of n1i ('number of deaths in the treatment group', 'number of patients in the treatment group') and ci of n2i (control) are each comparison's two arms as columns, one row per comparison; binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and the multiarm trials repeat their study label and control group ('Strictly speaking, there are only 31 trials, since Breddin et al. (1980) and ATACS (1990) are multiarm trials'); rma.mh pools subsets by intensity and aspirin use, and metadat holds no long form.

hcq_arm_event of hcq_arm_total and control_arm_event of control_arm_total are each trial's deaths and patients in its two arms as columns, one row per trial; binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, id ('registry number') also repeats for PROTECT A, B and C, and the page's escalc OR and rma per drug name no study level; metadat holds no long form.

id ('study number') never repeats, one standardized mean difference yi with vi per study; a few author names hold two studies of one year, attributes of distinct studies rather than an indexed unit, and rma and the meta-regressions on grade, length and the writing components put the study effect on single rows.

hsame, hdiff, tsame and tdiff are each person's flips cross-classified by landing and starting side as columns, one row per person; the page stacks each person's heads and same-side proportions ('restructure the dataset for a bivariate meta-analysis') and fits rma.mv(yi, V, mods = ~ 0 + outcome, random = ~ outcome | person, struct='UN'), so the long form is person x outcome, which metadat does not hold.

One standardized mean difference smd with se per study ('Results from 23 studies'); a few author labels recur for distinct studies and country is a study covariate, and rma (DL) and the single-moderator meta-regressions put the study effect on single rows.

One Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney statistic wmwstat with stderr per study ('five randomized, placebo-controlled studies'), study never repeating; rma.uni and bayesmeta put the study effect on single rows, and the studies' patients are dat.huber2000, in the registry.

b.xti, o.xti and d.xti of nti (treatment) and b.xci, o.xci and d.xci of nci (control) are each trial's bleeding, operation and death counts in its two arms as columns; the page's rma.glmm(model='CM.EL', method='ML') is the random-effects conditional logistic model ('fixed- and random-effects conditional logistic models') of the trial x arm long form, which metadat does not hold, and trial ('first author of trial') recurs for one author's two trials.

pre.xti of pre.nti and pre.xci of pre.nci, and the perinatal deaths, stillbirths and neonatal deaths of fup.nti and fup.nci, are each study's two arms as columns, one row per study; binomial counts stack into the study x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and rma.peto pools each outcome; metadat holds no long form.

One birth-prevalence count cases of total per study ('26 studies'), study ('first author, year') never repeating; country ('origin of investigated population') is a study covariate, and escalc PLN with rma.uni puts the study effect on single rows.

One mean difference mean with SE per cross-over study ('21 cross-over studies'), author with year never repeating (Skrabal et al. 1981a and 1981b are two studies); corr is the 'within-patient correlation', a study attribute, and metagen pools single rows.

xt of nt (treatment) and xc of nc (control) are each study's RTIs and patients in its two arms as columns, one row per study; binomial counts stack into the study x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and rma.mh and rma (DL) pool them; metadat holds no long form.

One proportion xi of ni per trial, the standard-care group's alone ('HAART-adherence in control groups'), author never repeating; scq, ethnicity, patients, select and sens are trial covariates of the rma meta-regressions, which put the trial effect on single rows.

x.a of n.a (active treatment) and x.p of n.p (placebo) are each trial's responders and participants in its two arms as columns, one row per trial; binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and escalc RR with rma (DL) pools them; metadat holds no long form.

ai of n1i (magnesium) and ci of n2i (control) are each trial's deaths and patients in its two arms as columns, id ('trial id number') unique though one author's trials share a study label; binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's and stan_bugs magnesium's arms, and rma.peto pools subsets; metadat holds no long form.

One prevalence depr of n per study ('19 studies'), author never repeating; region ('country'), design and the assessment columns are study covariates, and metaprop's random-effects model puts the study effect on single rows.

e1i to e4i (experimental) and c1i to c4i (control) are each trial's survivors at 6, 12, 18 and 24 months as columns, one row per trial; the page builds dat.long and fits rma.mv(yi, Vc, mods = ~ 0 + factor(time), random = ~ time | study, struct='HAR'), so the long form is trial x time, which metadat does not hold.

ai and bi (intervention) and ci and di (control) are the participants with and without days off work in each study's two arms as columns, which rma.mh(measure='RR') pools and which stack into the study x arm long form as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms; the m1i, sd1i, n1i and m2i, sd2i, n2i arm summaries alone would be flat, as HSAUR3 toothpaste's, and metadat holds no long form.
One adjusted log risk ratio b with SE per case-control study ('16 case-control studies'), author never repeating; metagen's common-effect model pools single rows, and no column indexes a unit.

study ('study number') never repeats, one log odds ratio yi with vi per study; a few first authors recur for distinct studies, country and design are study covariates, and rma (DL) puts the study effect on single rows.

One proportion xi of ni per study ('35 studies'), authorName unique (Vaira et al. 1 and 2 are two studies) and one DOI shared by an article's two studies; objectivity, country and patientType are study covariates, and rma overall and per objectivity subset puts the study effect on single rows.

x1i strokes over t1i person-years (warfarin) and x2i over t2i (control) are each trial's two arms as columns, one row per trial ('6 clinical trials'); the counts with their exposure stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and escalc IRR with rma pools them; metadat holds no long form.

tiotropium.exa to tiotropium.dropout of tiotropium.total and placebo.exa to placebo.dropout of placebo.total are each study's events per end point in its two arms as columns, one row per study; binomial counts stack into the study x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and escalc OR with bayesmeta pools them; metadat holds no long form.

tp of np (cases) and tn of nn (non-cases) are each study and patient group's sensitivity and specificity counts as columns; the page stacks the asymptomatic rows with to.long and fits rma.mv(yi, vi, mods = ~ 0 + group, random = ~ group | study, struct='UN'), so the long form is study x group, and a few study labels also hold both patient groups.

n.cbt.rec and n.cbt.non (CBT) and n.ctrl.rec and n.ctrl.non (control) are each program's recidivists and non-recidivists in its two arms as columns; binomial counts stack into the program x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and escalc OR with rma pools them; study ('(first) author and year') repeats for the few studies that give two programs, and metadat holds no long form.

ai of n1i (azithromycin) and ci of n2i (amoxycillin or amoxyclav) are each trial's clinical failures and patients in its two arms as columns, one row per trial; binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and rma.mh and rma pool them; metadat holds no long form.

ai of n1i (streptokinase) and ci of n2i (control) are each trial's deaths and patients in its two arms as columns, one row per trial; binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and rma.mh with its cumulative meta-analysis pools them; metadat holds no long form.

ai of n1i (treatment) and ci of n2i (sham) are each trial's patients with nausea in its two arms as columns, id ('trial id number') unique while first-author labels recur across trials; binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and rma(measure='RR') pools them; metadat holds no long form.

ai of n1i (magnesium) and ci of n2i (control) are each trial's deaths and patients in its two arms as columns, one row per trial ('similar to the dataset dat.egger2001'); binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and rma(measure='OR', method='EE') pools them; metadat holds no long form.

ai of n1i (hypericum) and ci of n2i (placebo) are each trial's responders and patients in its two arms as columns, one row per trial; binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and rma (DL) with group as moderator pools them; metadat holds no long form.

treatment1 to treatment3 with n1 to n3 and resp, remi, loss, loss.ae and ae per arm hold up to three arms of each trial as columns ('wide arm-based format'); the counts stack into the trial x arm long form in which metadat's arm-based network tables (dat.linde2016) are filed, and netmeta pools the pairwise() contrasts.

mean.das and mean.haq, with their limits, are each study's DAS-28 and HAQ mean differences as columns, one row per study; the page pools each outcome alone, but Bujkiewicz et al. (2014, Value in Health 17:109-115, pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3919215) fit a Bayesian multivariate random-effects meta-analysis of the HAQ and DAS-28 changes on Lloyd's studies, whose long form is study x outcome, which metadat does not hold.

Study ('Citation - Experiment - Subgroup') never repeats, one raw mean difference yi with vi per experiment or subgroup; No_brain_n, _m, _s and Brain_n, _m, _s are arm summaries, as HSAUR3 toothpaste's, McCabe and Castel's Experiment 3 splits into two critique rows with no column indexing the experiment, Participant_Pool is a recruitment source, and rma puts the effect on single rows.

One correlation ri with ni per study ('16 studies'), authors recurring only across years for distinct studies; rma on r-to-z puts the study effect on single rows, and design, the measures and quality are study covariates.

Ee of Ne (NSAIDS) and Ec of Nc (control) are each trial's treatment successes and patients in its two arms as columns, id ('study ID') unique; binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, metabin pools them, samecont ('same control group') marks the trials of one report that share a control arm (Aoki 1984), and metadat holds no long form.

ai of n1i (anti-infective catheter) and ci of n2i (standard catheter) are each study's CRBSIs and patients in its two arms as columns; the page's rma.glmm(model='CM.EL') is a random-effects conditional logistic model of the study x arm long form ('generalized linear mixed-effects models', Stijnen et al. 2010), which metadat does not hold.

x1i over t1i (anti-infective) and x2i over t2i (standard) are each study's CRBSIs and catheter days in its two arms as columns; the page's rma.glmm(measure='IRR', model='CM.EL') is a random-effects conditional Poisson model of the study x arm long form (Stijnen et al. 2010), which metadat does not hold.

treat.infarction and treat.death of treat.total and cont.infarction and cont.death of cont.total are each trial's two arms as columns; the page fits rma.glmm(model='UM.RS'), a binomial GLMM with random study effects of the trial x arm long form, which metadat holds as dat.tian2009 ('the same dataset, but with 6 additional trials'), filed in the registry, so this table is its wide subset.

Ne, Me, Se (mucolytic) and Nc, Mc, Sc (placebo) are the size, mean and SD of exacerbations per month in each trial's two arms, arm summaries rather than observations, as HSAUR3 toothpaste's; metacont by duration subgroup pools one difference per trial, and author labels recur only for distinct trials.

study ('study number') never repeats, one standardized mean difference yi with vi per study and weeks a covariate; Pellegrini & Hicks (1972) give an aware and a blind tester row under one author label, the table rabe_hesketh's expectancy.dta holds and was read flat, and rma puts the study effect on single rows.

TP of n1 (diseased) and TN of n2 (non-diseased), with FN and FP their complements, are each study's two reference groups as columns; metaprop pools TP of n1 and TN of n2 and metabin(TP, n1, n2-TN, n2) treats the groups as arms, so the counts stack into the study x group long form, as dat.kearon1998's, and SampleID repeats for one sample.

Ne, Me, Se (nedocromil) and Nc, Mc, Sc (placebo) are the size, mean and SD of the maximum FEV1 fall in each trial's two arms, arm summaries as HSAUR3 toothpaste's; metacont by agegroup pools one difference per trial, and author labels recur only for distinct trials (DeBenedictis 1994a, 1994b, 1995).
One log hazard ratio lnHR with selnHR per trial ('4 trials'), author never repeating; metagen's common-effect model pools single rows.

ai of n1i and ci of n2i are each trial's deaths or reinfarctions in its two arms as columns, one row per trial and outcome table (6, 9, 10, 11, 12a, 12b); binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, id ('trial id number') also repeats across the outcome tables of the long-term trials, rma.peto pools each table, and metadat holds no long form.

study_id ('unique id for study') and es_id are both unique over the rows, so no column indexes the '62 studies' the description names, and the effect sizes yi with vi enter an ordinary random-effects meta-analysis (hand check #162); population, task and stimulation are effect covariates.

factual and conceptual are each participant's memory scores on the two question types of one quiz as columns ('There were two types of questions, factual and conceptual questions'), overall their mean, one row per pid; talk ('TED talk seen by participant', five levels) is between participants, and Singmann's case study (stats_for_experiments, ch. 6) fits aov_car(conceptual ~ condition + Error(pid), laptop_urry), so no model stacks the scores and afex holds no long form.

COH01 to COH05 are each soldier's five cohesion items as columns, a person by item structure stored wide (carData DavisThin), with no soldier id; PLATOON ('Lower-level Platoon Identifier') holds a few soldiers each in 'four platoons further nested within two larger units', too few for a grouping factor the source does not fit, and the tutorial only demonstrates data manipulation.

One observer's detection trials, one row per trial with Contrast ('6 luminance contrast levels' and catch trials) and Stim fixed; Rating is the confidence rating, the response, and no column indexes a session or block.

One observer's '16 sessions of 224 trials', stored as the 32 noise samples N of each trial over time; the rows repeat within trials and sessions, but no column indexes either (datasets rock's unindexed cores), and MPDiR ch. 6 estimates the classification image by lm(N ~ time/resp - 1) without a random effect.

One observer's 2AFC trials from 'two randomly interleaved staircases'; StairCase has two levels, a design factor, and Trial ('the trial number for the staircase') numbers each staircase's own trials, so equal Trial values are different trials; MPDiR ch. 5 fits glm(Response ~ log10(Contrast), binomial(mafc.logit(2))).

One observer's counts NumUpward and NumDownward per cell of Phaseshift, WaveForm, TempFreq and Direction, fixed design factors; MPDiR ch. 4 fits glm(cbind(NumUpward, NumDownward) ~ Direction * WaveForm * TempFreq * Phaseshift, binomial) with several links, and no column indexes a unit.

fall_k, spring_k and spring_g1 are each student's reading scores in fall kindergarten, spring kindergarten and spring first grade as columns ('Wide dataset to be used for growth modeling'), studentid unique; MLMusingR holds no long form.

One row per day of one Capital Bikeshare series ('500 daily observations'); year, month, day_of_week and weekend are calendar indices, not units (datasets airquality, bambi_bikes), and Bayes Rules! fits rides by stan_glm without grouping.
One row per person; group classifies the 75 people into control and football players without and with concussion history, years counts the years played, and nothing repeats within a unit.

country ('country of origin') indexes the nationalities the artists repeat within, most holding several, as HSAUR3 Forbes2000's country holds its companies, while gender and department classify; Bayes Rules! (ch. 8) fits a Beta-Binomial of genx on moma_sample, a random sample of these artists, with no grouping. artist also repeats over departments with every other column constant, copies of one artist rather than repeated measures.

Daily weather at 'three Australian cities: Wollongong, Hobart, and Uluru', location a design factor of three levels; year, month and day_of_year are calendar indices of sampled days, not units, and Bayes Rules! enters location as a fixed predictor (chapter 11, on weather_WU).

y8 to y36 are each rat's weights on days 8, 15, 22, 29 and 36 as columns ('measured weekly over 5 weeks'), rat unique, and the page fits runMLwiN(c(y8, y15, y22, y29, y36) ~ 1 + (1 | rat), D = 'Multivariate Normal'); these are Gelfand et al.'s (1990) rats, whose long form posteriordb's rats_data.json.zip holds in the registry.
'Twenty rats were randomly assigned to a control condition or three doses of fluoxetine', one row per rat; dose is a fixed design factor, time.immob the response, and no column indexes a unit.
